fixes.explanation: That's right. “Behold, the Lord GOD comes with might, and His arm establishes His rule.” His arm is how He sets up His rule, and that's strength with a purpose. Say it with me, friend, because that verse has weight.

The wilderness is right. The voice says, “Prepare the way for the LORD in the wilderness…” It's not a spot with a nice view or a gift shop. The highway goes in the desert, and the work starts right there.

The glory of the LORD is right. The voice says, “And the glory of the LORD will be revealed…” After all that talk of valleys and mountains, here comes the big reveal. The text says all humanity together will see it.

Forever is right. “The grass withers and the flowers fall, but the word of our God stands forever.” The people are called grass, and their glory is like the flowers of the field (Isaiah 40:6–7). But the word of our God stands. That's the part to hold onto, friend.

Alone is an interesting guess, but the verse doesn't picture God's word that way. It says the word of our God “stands forever.” It's not about being by itself. It's set against the grass that withers and the flowers that fall.

Silent is a nice-sounding word, but it's not what the verse says. The verse says the word of our God “stands forever.” Forever is the word that matches the verse, friend. The grass withers and the flowers fall, but His word stands.
That's right. The herald is told to say to the cities of Judah, “Here is your God!” It's the whole message in four words. I think that's why it's worth shouting from a mountain.

I see why you picked it, because that's a message people would cheer for. But the text never gives it to the herald. The herald is told to say to the cities of Judah, “Here is your God!” The big news is about who is arriving.
A gardener tends things too, so I get why you picked it. But the verse names a flock, and a flock goes with a shepherd. The text says, “He tends His flock like a shepherd…” Different picture, friend.
False is right. The verse says, “He gently leads the nursing ewes.” That's how this shepherd treats them. After all that might in verse 10, this is a soft side of the same Lord GOD.
